subject: Maths
title: Equations involving fractions
subtitle: Fractions — Secondary · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can solve equations that contain algebraic fractions.

key_vocab.definition: An equation involving fractions has the unknown in a fraction. The key strategy is to multiply through by the LCD to eliminate denominators.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can solve equations that contain algebraic fractions.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: equation involving fractions -- An equation involving fractions has the unknown in a fraction. The key strategy is to multiply through by the LCD to eliminate denominators.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Multiply every term by the LCD to clear fractions, then solve the equation as normal.
&frac{x}{2} + &frac{x}{3} = 5 ⇒ 3x + 2x = 30
Multiply all terms by LCD = 6

Key examples:
  ✓ &frac{x}{3} = 5 ⇒ x = 15  (multiply both sides by 3)
  ✓ &frac{x}{2} + &frac{x}{3} = 5 ⇒ 5x = 30  (LCD = 6)
  ✓ &frac{2}{x} = &frac{1}{3} ⇒ x = 6  (cross-multiply)
  ✗ &frac{x}{2} + &frac{x}{3} = &frac{2x}{5}  (cannot add denominators)
  ✗ &frac{x+1}{3} = 5 ⇒ x = 14  (should be x + 1 = 15, x = 14 (correct!))

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – single fraction
  Solve &frac{x}{4} = 7
  Multiply both sides by 4
  x = 4 × 7
  x = 28
  x = 28
  (Multiply by the denominator to isolate x.)

Example 2 – two fractions
  Solve &frac{x}{2} + &frac{x}{5} = 7
  LCD = 10; multiply all terms by 10
  5x + 2x = 70
  7x = 70, so x = 10
  x = 10
  (After clearing fractions, collect terms and solve.)

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ To clear fractions, multiply every term by the LCD
✗ &frac{x}{2} + &frac{x}{3} = &frac{2x}{5}
✓ &frac{x+1}{3} = 5 gives x = 14
✗ &frac{6}{x} = 3 gives x = 18
✓ Cross-multiply means a/b = c/d gives ad = bc
